Performers
Collegium Vocale Bydgoszcz (vocal ensemble) Documented

Commons credits Collegium Vocale and links the CVBydgoszcz YouTube account. No director, individual singers or exact number of performers is confirmed by the available recording metadata.

[1] [2]
Work version
Four-part unaccompanied vocal chanson; exact performing edition unknown Documented

The inspected Smijers score has superius, contratenor, tenor and bassus, 41 bars. It supports texture and scoring, not a claim that this choir used that edition, its spelling or its pitch level.

[1] [4] [5]
Recorded
Unknown Unknown

Commons gives 24 September 2016 in its Date field, but does not establish that as the performance session. The 2017 MQS description and 3 January 2018 Commons import are also not session dates.

[1] [2] [3]
Place
Unknown Unknown

Bydgoszcz identifies the ensemble, not a documented recording location.

[1]
Label
Unknown Unknown

No original commercial label is established. The page’s MQS edition description is not treated as an original recording imprint.

[1]
Catalogue
Unknown Unknown

No release catalogue number is supplied.

[1]
Matrix, take, sides
Unknown Unknown

Original medium and session take identification are not documented.

[1]
Transfer
Imported from YouTube by Paterm to Wikimedia Commons Documented

This credits the known import, not an unverified recording, production or mastering engineer.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

Commons import was 3 January 2018, and the current MP3 transcode is dated 25 February 2026. Neither establishes when the original performance was recorded or mastered.

[1]
Processing
YouTube audio imported as Opus; Wikimedia MP3 access transcode Documented

The source embeds Lavf57.25.100. Earlier encoding, editing, noise reduction, pitch correction and production settings remain unknown. No additional processing or trim by Contrapunctus.

[1]
Composition rights
Historical chanson outside ordinary composition copyright terms Inferred, not documented

The authorship dispute does not make the sixteenth-century composition a modern work. This does not confer any rights in the Collegium Vocale recording.

[4] [5] [6]
Recording rights
Rule 1 — CC BY 3.0 Unported as explicitly declared for the recording on Commons Documented

The YouTube CC-BY template credits Collegium Vocale and expressly concerns this audio import, not merely the composition. Commons still marks external licence review as pending. The original YouTube page and its linked Wayback capture were opened but did not expose a usable source licence; independent confirmation of the former YouTube setting is therefore unavailable. The nominated recording is retained with that limitation visible, not described as licence-review approved.

[1] [7]

Mille regretz, traditionally attributed to Josquin des Prez; performed by Collegium Vocale Bydgoszcz. YouTube import by Paterm, Wikimedia Commons. Recording declared CC BY 3.0 Unported; external licence review remains pending. MP3 access derivative, no new editorial audio cut. Rights statement

  2. Collegium Vocale — nominated YouTube source — Source identified by the Commons import. Opened, but no usable source description or licence was exposed; not independent confirmation of licensing or session metadata.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  3. Wayback capture of the nominated YouTube source — Capture linked by Commons; opened and returned video unavailable. No independently viewable historical licence was obtained.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  4. IMSLP — Mille regretz, attributed to Josquin — Attribution discussion, catalogue number, four-part scoring, Smijers edition imprint and public-domain status.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  5. Mille regretz — Smijers score scan, imprint discrepancy — One-page score, printed p. 63, No. 24, 41 bars; viewed in full. Footer reads 28032, differing from IMSLP’s catalogued plate 16845. Four parts, central intensification and extended final textual sentence.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  6. Mille regretz — text and attribution overview — Four-line French poem of separation and regret; authorship controversy. Biographical and imperial anecdotes are not promoted into public claims.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
